sources.name: CEPR — The economics of the Kalshi prediction market (300k+ contracts)
sources.use: Supports the favorite-longshot roster design: 5-20c contracts underperform their price, 80-95c favorites overperform; taker longshot losses far larger than maker losses
sources.note: Research context for SureThing/YieldSniper and the documented DipHunter failure mode. It does not verify any price, fill or settlement in this repository.

sources.name: r/PredictionsMarkets — 5,000 strategies backtested on Kalshi 15-min BTC markets
sources.use: Hypothesis for a future season: volatility-reversion ('panic fade') was the only profitable archetype; tight 2c high-turnover targets are fee/slippage traps; 0.10-0.40 mean-reversion entries were 0-for-432
sources.note: The KXBTC15M series was independently observed on the verified official trade tape (trade-tape-sample.csv). No numbers from the post are used; a future session must re-verify against the official KXBTC15M tape before any claim.

sources.name: r/PredictionsMarkets — 'Shock-timing' World Cup bot (+39% claim) and its backtest refutation
sources.use: Example of a community return claim failing out-of-sample re-testing (panic-fade and sell-the-bounce variants lose); kept to calibrate skepticism toward social results
sources.note: Discovery reference only. Neither the +39% claim nor the refutation is accepted as evidence; both are social posts.

sources.name: Academic synthesis of prediction-market strategy literature
sources.use: Framing: buying NO on overpriced longshots is the long-only expression of the favorite-longshot edge; passive liquidity provision on Kalshi shows aggregate positive returns (with event-risk caveats)
sources.note: Discovery context for the YieldSniper thesis and the maker-side research path (SpreadSmith remains gated).

sources.name: Optimal Market Making in Prediction Markets (stochastic control)
sources.use: Theoretical quoting rules for binary-settlement market making (spread/skew vs inventory and time-to-resolution); a public referee note flags one unsupported downside-protection claim
sources.note: Research path for future maker-fee-aware quote modeling; not a price or fill source.

irregularities: IRR-01 · Live data is intentionally fail-closed: an API/network/CORS failure produces an empty market panel, not demo quotes.
IRR-02 · This static page has public read access only. It never submits live orders and cannot verify queue position or a real fill.
IRR-03 · Kalshi's binary order book returns bids; reciprocal asks are derived from the opposing bid and visibly labelled.
IRR-04 · Fee type and multiplier can vary by series. The local paper estimate uses the published standard quadratic formula unless a future series adapter supplies an override.
IRR-05 · Browser localStorage is not a shared server database. Export JSON/CSV and run a scheduled collector before treating the competition as a durable one-year record.
IRR-06 · User project pages, social posts and contest sites are discovery/research references only; none can verify an exchange fill.

IRR-07 · (superseded 2026-09-20) A verified candlestick archive is now bundled under data/season-2026/ (SHA-256 bound, cross-checked by scripts/verify_data.py) and the Backtest section publishes results from it. Only bars from stored official responses are used; the KXFED full-history window beyond the stored 90 days is still not archived.
IRR-08 · The CEO label was not resolvable to a MasterSite entry during review, so it remains an explicit unresolved item instead of a guessed link.

IRR-09 · Kalshi's current API reference shows authentication headers for the orderbook endpoint while its getting-started response guide says no authentication is required; this app uses no credentials and treats a rejected public read as unavailable.

IRR-10 · A live response read on 2026-09-19 returned status=active for rows selected by the status=open query; the app accepts both open and active and retains the raw status in each observation/trade record.

IRR-11 · Backtest fee model: the published taker fee 0.07·q·p·(1-p) is applied at entry and verified bid exits, rounded up to $0.0001 (Kalshi fee-rounding docs). No fee is modeled at settlement — flagged as an assumption pending settlement-fee documentation; KXFED/KXCPI are quadratic_with_maker_fees series and taker fills use the standard formula, maker-side differences are not modeled.

IRR-12 · This build was collected from a sandbox without direct egress to kalshi.com: official responses were read via a server-side reader and transcribed into the committed CSV/JSON files. Mitigations: 50 automated cross-checks (volume sums equal market-record volume exactly, open-interest continuity, timestamp monotonicity, price bounds, settlement fields) plus SHA-256 binding. A future collector with direct API access should re-fetch the same URLs and diff byte-for-byte; single-field transcription errors remain a residual risk.

IRR-13 · No gold/commodity price feed was reachable from this environment on 2026-09-19 (FRED CSV URL returned an error page; Stooq returned 'Access denied'). No gold price is stored or used anywhere; MetalMomentum remains source-gated with manual review links.

IRR-14 · The official /markets/trades endpoint ignored the market_ticker filter in the captured call, so the committed trade-tape sample spans multiple tickers (recorded as all-market). The per-market trade filter parameter name is not verified and is not used.
